newsitem.title: USA: Mirage Q2 earnings led by strong showing at flagship.
newsitem.headline: Mirage Q2 earnings led by strong showing at flagship.

text.p: Mirage Resorts Inc., one of the nation's largest gambling companies, said Tuesday its second-quarter net income rose to $48.9 million as its flagship hotel thrived despite growing competition.
The hotel, the Mirage in Las Vegas, saw its revenues climb 13 percent to $202 million and operating income jump 33 percent to $57 million from the year-ago second quarter.
Overall company revenues rose about 10 percent to $344 million from $312 million last year. Earnings per share grew to 26 cents, as analysts had expected, from 21 cents in the 1996 second quarter.
Mirage shares closed down 37.5 cents at $24.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.

The company noted the increase in earnings came amid a highly competitive Las Vegas market. It cited a tourist authority as saying the number of available guest rooms rose by 12.9 percent from January to April while tourist traffic climbed only 5.7 percent, compared with last year's figures.

Despite the rising number of hotel rooms, Mirage was able to maintain an occupancy rate of 99 percent vs. 99.6 percent last year, and its average room rate in Las Vegas rose to $95 a night from $92 a night.

Mirage owns three hotel-casinos in Las Vegas, The Mirage, Treasure Island and Golden Nugget, and it owns Golden Nugget-Laughlin in Laughlin, Nev. It also has a 50 percent share of the Monte Carlo hotel-casino in Las Vegas.
